breakdown.description: The prompt uses the polar moment J in the Euler buckling formula, even though Euler buckling depends on the flexural second moment I.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'Use the polar moment of inertia J = πd⁴/32 as the second moment of area I,' repeating the original error. It uses I = πd⁴/32 = 79521.56 mm⁴ instead of the correct second moment of area I = πd⁴/64 = 39760.78 mm⁴. The ground truth removes this incorrect instruction entirely, relying on the standard Euler formula with the correct I.

breakdown.description: The prompt multiplies the critical load by the factor of safety to obtain the allowable load, whereas the allowable load should be the critical load divided by the factor of safety.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly computes P_allow = P_cr/n = 1742.4/2.0 = 871.2 N, dividing the critical load by the factor of safety rather than multiplying, which aligns with the ground truth.
